close_reason: Resolved together: all 6 FileNode/* handlers now consult supports_type::<FileNode>() at the top and return accountNotSupportedByMethod when the backend has opted out. Mirrors canonical jmap-mail-server snippet.rs:35 pattern. Regression test all_handlers_gate_on_supports_type_false uses a NoFileNodeBackend wrapper (mirroring NoSnippetBackend in mail-server tests/integration.rs:490).
description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/lib.rs:75-116

```rust
pub fn register_filenode_handlers<B>(
    dispatcher: &mut Dispatcher<B::CallerCtx>,
    backend: Arc<B>,
)
where
    B: FileNodeBackend + 'static,
{
    // ... reg!("FileNode/get", ...);
    // ... reg!("FileNode/set", ...);
    // ... six method names registered unconditionally ...
}
```

Companion bead to JMAP-510h.34 (supports_type dead method). This
finding is the call-site half: even if a backend declares
`fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool { false }` for
FileNode (intent: this deployment does NOT support the FileNode
extension), `register_filenode_handlers` will STILL register all
six method handlers. The dispatcher will route `FileNode/get` calls
into the handler, which will then call `backend.get_objects()` —
a fully-typed call that succeeds in the type system but produces
unspecified runtime results.

The function name and signature suggest "register the handlers for
this extension". It does not say "register unconditionally".

Compare canonical sibling jmap-mail-server: `snippet.rs:35` performs
the gate check INSIDE the handler. That works because
`SearchSnippet/get` is one method; for the six FileNode methods,
checking `supports_type::<FileNode>()` six times inside six handler
bodies is duplication. The cleaner gate is at registration time.

Three resolution paths:

1. **Eager gate at registration:**
   ```rust
   pub fn register_filenode_handlers<B>(...)  -> Result<(), NotSupportedError>
   where B: FileNodeBackend + 'static,
   {
       if !backend.supports_type::<FileNode>() {
           return Err(NotSupportedError);
       }
       // ... registrations ...
       Ok(())
   }
   ```
   Breaking the signature change. The fix is principled but
   propagates through every consumer of `register_filenode_handlers`.

2. **Silent skip with diagnostic log line.** Less principled but
   non-breaking.

3. **Document the actual behaviour.** Add to the doc: "This function
   registers all six handler endpoints unconditionally. If the
   backend's `supports_type::<FileNode>()` returns false, calls to
   the registered methods will still execute against the backend
   and produce whatever result the backend chooses to return."

Right now the function is at #3 but with no doc — defensive-code-
forcing on every consumer who has to read the source to know.

Propagation note: this is the inverse of JMAP-510h.34. Either pair
of resolutions must land together: if `supports_type` is removed,
this finding is moot; if `supports_type` is honored at the handler
seam (canonical's pattern), this finding becomes "do that for all
six FileNode handlers"; if `supports_type` is honored at the
registration seam (my path 1), this finding becomes "do it once
for the family".

`api-contract,defensive` because every backend implementor today
must implement a method that the registration call ignores. The
asymmetry is the foot-gun.
title: register_filenode_handlers registers all 6 methods even when backend.supports_type::<FileNode>() returns false
